target_customer: Fast shipping software and product engineering teams (named customers include Bilt, Arize, Vial, 11x)
problem: Teams cannot watch thousands of session replays or maintain brittle end-to-end tests, so bugs reach users unnoticed.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for AI session replay analysis and AI QA test generation
product_category: Developer tools: AI QA and session replay analysis

founders.name: Michael Rosenfield
founders.background_notes: Senior product manager at Google; led the first native ads format on Google Maps and Pixel premium tier product.

founders.name: Rohan Das
founders.background_notes: Staff engineer and manager on the YouTube Homepage; led a rebuild of the Homepage service.

technical_complexity.rationale: Applying LLMs to session replay data and generating self healing browser tests needed reliable agent behavior, standard engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Many funded startups attacked AI testing at once and the underlying models were available to all; switching costs come only from stored tests and integrations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy found in sources; QA competitors such as Momentic and QA.tech raised seed rounds in 2024 to 2025.

market_need_then: Session replay volume is too high to review by hand and E2E test maintenance is a known cost; the company's own blog and a customer case study (11x) cite this, no independent spend data found.

branding.domain_note: getdecipher.com with a get prefix; the root site fetched returned 404 at one URL.

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer focused blog tone, for example Of course you don't watch session replays

branding.community_and_virality: Content marketing via company blog and a launch week in April 2025; no meme or fan coverage found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is a common word shared with several unrelated Decipher products, so searches mix them up; no press on the brand itself.

pivots.from: AI agent that watches session replays and monitors errors
pivots.to: AI QA agent that generates and maintains end-to-end tests
pivots.why: The company's blog says it built AI testing as coding agents made shipping faster; exact date not confirmed

outcome_analysis: Decipher AI started in YC Winter 2024 as an AI session replay analysis tool and later repositioned toward AI QA testing as its YC copy now states. It remains Active with a small team and named startup customers, but only a 500K pre-seed from a single aggregator is reported, so scale is unverified. The AI QA market became crowded with funded rivals, which is the main risk.
notes: Funding: aggregators (VCBacked, CB Insights) list a 500K pre-seed around April 2024 with YC and BoxGroup, CB Insights says convertible note; unverified single-source so not recorded as a round. A Signalbase page describes the company differently. Competitor results were 2026 guides with no dated 2024 sources, so the list is empty by rule. Founded year per YC is 2023. Update: the 500K pre-seed is now recorded as a round from VCBacked (dated 2024-04, YC and BoxGroup); CB Insights lists it as a convertible note dated 2024-01-01 and names BoxGroup, so the date conflicts. It rests on databases only, no press or filing.
